Evans-Jensen lecture classification: 2

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A two-part intertrochanteric fracture is displaced but can regain stable cortical contact after reduction. Using the supplied lecture’s grade 1A and 1B notation, which category describes this displaced two-part fracture pattern?

  1. Grade 1B in the supplied lecture scheme
  2. Grade 1A in the supplied lecture scheme
  3. Grade 2A in the supplied lecture scheme
  4. Grade 2B in the supplied lecture scheme
  5. Grade 3 in the supplied lecture scheme
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Grade 1B in the supplied lecture scheme

A displaced two-part intertrochanteric fracture is grade 1B; it can be stable after adequate reduction.

Understanding the options

Grade 1B in the supplied lecture scheme
A displaced two-part intertrochanteric fracture is grade 1B; it can be stable after adequate reduction.
Grade 1A in the supplied lecture scheme
A two-part nondisplaced intertrochanteric fracture is grade 1A in this lecture’s Evans-Jensen notation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Grade 2A in the supplied lecture scheme
A three-part fracture with a separate greater trochanter is grade 2A in this notation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Grade 2B in the supplied lecture scheme
A three-part fracture with a separate lesser trochanter is grade 2B in this notation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Grade 3 in the supplied lecture scheme
A four-part intertrochanteric pattern is grade 3 in the supplied lecture scheme. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
